name: cross-reflection
context: Multi-agent systems where two or more agents or models provide reflective feedback on each other's plans or outputs before execution. Unlike debate (which is adversarial and converges through argument), cross-reflection is cooperative — agents share critiques to strengthen each other's reasoning before a final decision is made.
benefits: Catches blind spots that a single agent's self-reflection misses
Different agent perspectives surface implicit assumptions in the plan
Improves reasoning certainty by requiring explicit justification to a critic
Works without an explicit evaluator or rubric — criticism emerges from diversity
tradeoffs: Requires multiple agents or models capable of genuine critique
Can deadlock if agents continuously reject each other's revisions without resolution
Higher token cost than single-agent self-reflection
Quality depends on critic agents having relevant domain knowledge
use_cases: Strategic planning: a planner agent and a risk agent cross-review a proposed course of action
Research: two agents with different source expertise critique each other's literature interpretations
Legal reasoning: a facts agent and a law agent cross-review each other's analysis before a brief
Code review: an implementation agent and a security agent cross-check before a change is approved
avoid_when: Only one agent has relevant expertise — cross-reflection adds no signal
Time pressure requires immediate single-pass response
Agents do not have sufficient context about each other's domain to critique effectively
technology_stack: CrewAI sequential agents with critique steps
anti_patterns: Having critics with identical perspectives — no new information is generated
No mechanism to resolve persistent disagreement — loops indefinitely
Critique without actionable revision — agents identify problems but do not fix them
design_principles: Critic agents must have a distinct expertise or perspective from the proposer
Critiques must be actionable — vague criticism without revision paths is noise
The loop must have a defined exit condition (consensus, vote, or max iterations)
best_practices: Structure critique around specific questions (does the plan handle edge case X?)
Limit the number of cross-reflection rounds to prevent infinite loops
Combine cross-reflection with a final synthesizer agent that integrates revisions
references: Lu et al., Agent Design Pattern Catalogue, 2024 (arXiv:2405.10467) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.10467
